lines.speaker: erinome
lines.text: Dale, thanks for jumping on. I have the monthly P and L and the add-back ledger in front of me, and I need to walk a few lines with you before this goes to committee. I'm recording for the file.

lines.speaker: alnilam
lines.text: Understood. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: erinome
lines.text: Start at the top. Trailing twelve month revenue.

lines.speaker: alnilam
lines.text: Fourteen million, two hundred thousand.

lines.speaker: erinome
lines.text: And EBITDA. Because I am looking at two different numbers. Your CIM and your teaser both say three million, one hundred thousand. The audited ledger you sent Friday says two million, one hundred and fifty thousand.

lines.speaker: alnilam
lines.text: [hesitates] Right. The, ah, the three point one is the adjusted figure. The two million one fifty is what the audit supports.

lines.speaker: erinome
lines.text: So the gap is nine hundred and fifty thousand.

lines.speaker: alnilam
lines.text: That's the add-back stack, yes.

lines.speaker: erinome
lines.text: Walk me through the stack. What is actually in it?

lines.speaker: alnilam
lines.text: [clears throat] There's owner compensation normalisation. Some one-time legal from the twenty twenty-four dispute. The ERP implementation. And there are some vehicle leases in there.

lines.speaker: erinome
lines.text: Vehicle leases. Whose vehicles?

lines.speaker: alnilam
lines.text: [pause] They're leased through the company. Two of them are Mister Vanguard's. A Range Rover and a Porsche Cayenne. There's a third one for his son.

lines.speaker: erinome
lines.text: Are any of those vehicles used in the business?

lines.speaker: alnilam
lines.text: Not operationally, no. The shop trucks are separate. Those sit on a different line.

lines.speaker: erinome
lines.text: So we have personal luxury vehicle leases sitting inside the seller's add-backs, presented to us as EBITDA.

lines.speaker: alnilam
lines.text: That is how the bridge was built, yes. And I'll be honest with you, I flagged it internally. Along with the family travel, and two family members on the payroll who I could not tell you what they do day to day. All in, that's about four hundred and fifty thousand of the nine fifty.

lines.speaker: erinome
lines.text: I appreciate the straight answer. That four hundred and fifty thousand comes out. It's a personal expense the buyer would eliminate, but we don't credit it back into earnings the way your bridge does.

lines.speaker: alnilam
lines.text: I understand the argument.

lines.speaker: erinome
lines.text: Second item. The machinery inspection came back with deferred spindle work across the CNC fleet. The range they gave us is four hundred and eighty thousand to eight hundred thousand.

lines.speaker: alnilam
lines.text: That's a fair range. We have pushed the spindle rebuilds two years running to protect cash.

lines.speaker: erinome
lines.text: Third. Your top customer is thirty-eight and a half percent of revenue, five million, four hundred and seventy thousand. And I'm holding an email saying the long-term agreement expires April thirtieth and goes out to competitive bid with a fifteen percent price reduction demand.

lines.speaker: alnilam
lines.text: That is accurate.

lines.speaker: erinome
lines.text: Then we are not paying fourteen point two. On two million one fifty of supportable earnings we're in a nine point two to ten and a half million range. I'll send the revised bridge tonight.

lines.speaker: alnilam
lines.text: I'll take it to him.
